name: Boiled Apple Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: fine juicy apples
ingredients.originalText: two pounds of fine juicy apples

ingredients.name: quarter of a pound of brown sugar
ingredients.originalText: a quarter of a pound of brown sugar

ingredients.name: juice and yellow peel of a large lemon
ingredients.originalText: juice and yellow peel of a large lemon

instructions.text: Pare, core, and quarter as many fine juicy apples as will weigh two pounds when done
Strew among them a quarter of a pound of brown sugar
Add a grated nutmeg, and the juice and yellow peel of a large lemon
Prepare a paste of suet and flour, in the proportion of a pound of chopped suet to two pounds of flour
Roll it out of moderate thickness
Lay the apples in the centre, and close the paste nicely over them in the form of a large dumpling
Tie it in a cloth and boil it three hours
Send it to table hot, and eat with it cream sauce, or with butter and sugar
Ensure the water boils before the pudding goes in

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Pare, core, and quarter as many fine juicy apples as will weigh two pounds when done
2. Strew among them a quarter of a pound of brown sugar
3. Add a grated nutmeg, and the juice and yellow peel of a large lemon
4. Prepare a paste of suet and flour, in the proportion of a pound of chopped suet to two pounds of flour
5. Roll it out of moderate thickness
6. Lay the apples in the centre, and close the paste nicely over them in the form of a large dumpling
7. Tie it in a cloth and boil it three hours
8. Send it to table hot, and eat with it cream sauce, or with butter and sugar
9. Ensure the water boils before the pudding goes in
